model.convention: Q is a column-generator; Q[j,i]=q_{i->j} for j != i; Q[i,i]=-sum_{j != i} q_{i->j}.
model.observations: For each randomized pure start e_i and fixed treatment, measure all K phenotype fractions and absolute total N(tau)/N(0) at one time tau; the within-replicate product gives normalized state counts whose expectation is column i of exp((Q+diag(r))*tau).
model.independent_unit: independent well or founder inoculation, not descendant cells
model.unidentified_from_mean_interface: birth and death separately; only net r_i is represented

claims.name: Full-K one-lag global identification
claims.statement: For K>=3, one unrestricted finite-time endpoint matrix, even from all K pure starts with exact fractions and absolute totals, does not globally identify all switching rates and net growth rates.
claims.proof: Three-state irreducible circulant cycle: fix s=u+v and shift d=u-v by 4*pi/(sqrt(3)*tau); shared Fourier eigenvectors and eigenvalue imaginary shifts +/-2*pi/tau give identical exp(tau Q) for distinct positive rate pairs. For K>3, block-diagonal embedding refutes the full allowed class.
claims.finite_check: At tau=1, pairs (5,5) and (8.6275987285,1.3724012715) have max endpoint matrix difference 2.34e-15 and max generator difference 3.6276.
claims.limits: For K>3 the embedded example is reducible; no claim is made for every larger-K irreducible subclass or for parameter boxes that provably exclude aliases.

claims.name: Two-state exact endpoint recovery
claims.statement: For K=2, exact M(tau)=exp(tau A) identifies any admissible 2x2 Metzler A; its spectrum is real and A is recovered by the principal logarithm.
claims.proof: A 2x2 Metzler matrix has discriminant (a-d)^2+4bc>=0; the real exponential is injective on its eigenvalues, with the repeated/Jordan case also uniquely inverted.

claims.name: No-alias recovery for general K
claims.statement: If tau*||A||_1<pi, K linearly independent known initial mixtures recover M and the principal logarithm recovers A; then q_{i->j}=A_{ji} and r_i=sum_j A_{ji}.
claims.sufficient_bound: If |r_i|<=R and sum_{j!=i}q_{i->j}<=Lambda for all i, ||A||_1<=R+2*Lambda.

claims.name: Number of independent initial conditions
claims.statement: K linearly independent known initial mixtures are necessary for a uniform all-rates guarantee; K pure starts are sufficient only with an injectivity/no-alias condition.
claims.counterexample: With fewer than K pure starts, a source state can be made unreachable from all observed starts; changing its outgoing rates leaves all observed endpoint columns unchanged.

claims.name: Absolute totals separate switching from net growth
claims.statement: Fraction-only endpoints can alias switching and relative growth even with all pure starts; absolute endpoint totals recover the column scales needed to form M.
claims.counterexample: At tau=1, one-way rate q=1,r=(0,0) and q'=e-1,r'=(e-2,-1) have identical fractions from both pure starts but different total from state-1 start.

claims.name: Finite-time first-order rate error
claims.statement: For ||A||_1<=B, R_tau=exp(B*tau)-1-B*tau, and entrywise endpoint error <=epsilon_M, the estimator (Mhat-I)/tau has off-diagonal rate error <=(epsilon_M+R_tau)/tau; net-growth error <=(K*epsilon_M+R_tau)/tau.
claims.finite_check: Cycle script verifies the observed max off-diagonal error is below the analytic finite-tau remainder bound for its test instance.

claims.name: Bounded-well sample complexity
claims.statement: For A0 actions, K pure starts, n independent wells per action/start, unbiased normalized count coordinates in [0,C], probability of any endpoint mean coordinate error above epsilon_M is at most 2*A0*K^2*exp(-2*n*epsilon_M^2/C^2).
claims.limitation: The expected-count ODE alone supplies no concentration law. Unbounded branching counts require a specified tail/variance/likelihood model; clipping bias must be added.

claims.name: Finite-action robust reach-avoid
claims.statement: For state-level CTMC reach-avoid by horizon H and a coordinate confidence radius epsilon_q on off-diagonal rates, action value differs from its center by at most 2*H*(K-1)*epsilon_q; maximizing lower bounds is a finite-action maximin rule.
claims.limitation: The mean-count ODE does not define lineage branching/extinction probabilities. Population reach-avoid needs an explicit branching and censoring model.

claims.name: Biological validity and practical superiority
claims.statement: The one-lag linear model, rate bounds, independent-well observation law, and robust policy are valid or practically superior in a particular cell system.
claims.falsifier: Reject the fixed homogeneous Markov model if independent multi-lag data violate semigroup consistency M(t+s)=M(t)M(s) beyond calibration, no admissible bounded generator fits, or lineage data show history-dependent switching, treatment/time variation, impure starts, reporter confusion, or unmodeled proliferation/censoring.

claims.name: Novelty/priority
claims.statement: The embedding counterexample, pure-start requirement, short-time bounds, sample design, active time selection, or finite-action robust policy is new relative to prior art.
claims.reason: The core ambiguity is the classical Markov embedding problem; CellTrans uses a full-rank initial composition matrix; Transcompp and Gunnarsson et al. handle multi-time transition/growth inference; KCA/tree-HMM exploit lineage pedigrees; ICML 2026 directly studies active timepoint selection for measure-valued trajectories.

excluded_unless_supplied: biological acquisition of B, R, Lambda, or confidence sets
rate measurement model beyond the stated bounded-support assumption
sorting failure, batch effects, shared-well dependence, and assay saturation
lineage imaging/sequencing costs for stronger controls
extra destructive cohorts for multiple time points

prior_art.work: Baake and Sumner, The embedding problem for Markov matrices
prior_art.relevance: Classical generator/matrix-exponential embedding and multiple admissible Markov generators.
Full-rank starting composition matrix, pure starts, transition inference from proportions; equal/similar growth focus.
Multi-time snapshot fitting with optional state-specific proliferation and uncertainty estimates.
Stochastic division/death/switching inference from fraction or absolute-count data at one or more times; likelihood confidence intervals and identifiability analysis.

prior_art.work: Hormoz et al. 2016, kin correlation analysis
prior_art.relevance: Lineage-pedigree correlations and endpoint labels infer cell-state transition networks.
Uses lineage trees and handles transition/division/censoring structure.

prior_art.work: Huynh and van der Schaar, ICML 2026, Active Timepoint Selection for Learning Measure-Valued Trajectories
prior_art.relevance: Direct active timepoint-selection prior art for sparse/destructive distribution-valued trajectory measurements.

checks: positive three-state generators have matching endpoint matrices to floating-point tolerance
two-start unreachable-source counterexample matches on observed columns
finite-tau bias bound holds for the test instance
near-identity logarithm reconstructs A to below 3e-14 max error
grid sample planner and cost accounting return valid JSON
robust finite-action rule reports overlapping intervals and no false unique/threshold guarantee
execution.scope: finite numerical checks only; no general proof or biological validation
